reading.body:
Resemble AI builds detection systems for AI-generated audio, video, and images, positioning itself in the trust and verification layer of synthetic media rather than creation tools.

The company's market exists because voice cloning and deepfake video calls have become fraud vectors at scale. FBI data cited in the context around this company places business email compromise losses involving AI voice at over three billion dollars in 2025, a two hundred fifty million dollar increase year over year. Detection of synthetic media is not a peripheral concern but a response to specific, quantified harm in enterprise operations.

Resemble AI's architecture choice, a world model designed to recognize physical impossibilities rather than pattern-matching alone, reflects a technical bet that detection requires reasoning about what the real world permits. The company offers deployment flexibility, on-premises or cloud, which matters for customers with data sensitivity around the media they need analyzed. Neither product launch velocity, customer count, nor financial performance is covered in this data, leaving the question of detection accuracy and adoption rate unresolved.

profile_text.body:
Resemble AI is a Toronto-based company founded in 2018 that describes itself as focused on multimodal deepfake detection and watermarking for enterprise customers. Its site states the company powers real-time detection of AI-generated audio, video, and images, with deployment options on-premises or in the cloud. The company describes its core detection product, DETECT-World, as combining pattern matching and training with a world model architecture designed to recognize deviations from physical reality.

The company positions itself at the intersection of AI content creation and trust verification, offering media verification tools intended to help enterprises satisfy AI content compliance standards and prevent fraud. Its site notes that Resemble AI won the T Challenge competition organized by T-Mobile US and Deutsche Telekom in 2025. The held facts also record a tracked product under the voice and audio category, described as involving voice cloning with associated likeness and consent risk, reflecting an earlier or parallel focus on generative voice technology alongside its detection work.

No litigation or SEC filings appear in the held facts for Resemble AI. The site's surrounding context draws heavily on reported incidents of deepfake-enabled fraud and abuse, including cases cited from FBI data published by Forbes indicating that business email compromise scams attributed in part to AI voice cloning and deepfake video calls stole over $3 billion in 2025, a figure the company uses to frame the market need for its detection products.
